Have you used a similar road-condition or navigation application before?
column5: Q1:  In your own words, what do you think the risk score and the green, orange, and red colour coding mean?
column6: S1:  The detection results were easy to understand.
column7: S2:  The risk score and category - low, medium, or high - were intuitive.
column8: S3:  The map made it clear which roads were risky.
column9: S4:  I would trust the system's risk assessment.
column10: S5:  The route comparison was useful for deciding which way to go.
column11: Q1:  What was confusing or unclear while using the application?
column12: Q2:  Would you trust an automated system like this to influence your route choice? Why or why not?
column13: Q3:  What would make this application more useful to you?
column14: Q4:  Do you have any other comments or suggestions?

column5:
The green means risk-free road segment.
The yellow is medium risk road segment.
The red is the most dangerous road segment.
The black is not classified road segment.
column11: Some of the buttons are not clearly visible.
column12: Yes, I would trust, because that we have unbiased evaluation of the road conditions and to chose the safest route.
column13:
I would make it more useful when there will be a way to filter the markers based on their date, and can filter the older and the most recent one.
There is also not a way to delete the markers that are maybe fixed one day.
I personally can use this system to indicate problems on the road, but it will be more useful if there is automated indication of the municipality responsible for the roads near the damaged segment.
column14:
It will be useful if you can automate the process of uploading new road damaged segments. It can be useful if it gets the input from car video recorder which always records and scan the road, and can run all the collected videos through the pipeline.


Also another question for me is if I go through a road that is already scanned, how can I indicate if the segment is repaired.

column5:
The risk score is the evaluation of the risk of the road.
The green, orange, and red means the risk damage by low, medium, high.
column11: Nothing besides the button colours were confusing.
column12: I would trust a system like this because I find it reliable and want to avoid road damages that can cause problem to my car. And don’t want to lower the speed because of potholes and road damages that are risky.
column13: It will be useful if it can be somehow connected to the gps location and to easily notify when you are approaching a high risk road segment.
column14:
The damage class can be easily displayed via short notification identifying what damage is approaching whether its high, low or medium, or approaching pothole, or any kind of crack.
It can be indicated by combining the first letters of each road type and maybe got it as notification on the device used.

column5:
When I checked images from all colourings on the damage map I saw that the green represents low risk, yellow-medium risk, red-high risk roads. There is also one additional black which is for images uploaded without detections.
The risk score as I can see for images with more damages detected is higher, so I think based on all the damage on the road segment the risk is combined and multiplied.
column11: Something I find confusing when using the map was that on the safer route planner page I found an adjustable variable called alpha for risk-aversion strength, which is not clear what it's used for.
column12: It depends on the thresholds set. As I saw the detection confidence for some images and classes is low, which I wouldn't trust. Overall the app looks great, with great purpose and will be useful it for the classes that have highest confidence.
column13: The application will be more useful if it has something like a guide with deep explanations what is the function for every thresholds that can be set.
column14: Overall, I think the application function is great. The UI can be a bit more visually appealing but for a prototype app it's also really good, and most importantly showing that everything is working perfectly.

column5:
The risk score shown displays the cumulative risk of the road, because when I compared red and green segments, I saw that the red has highest risk because of the higher amount of damages and more dangerous classes.
I think the green means low risk risk road, the yellow medium risk, and the red - high risk.
column11: One unclear and confusing thing that I found was that on the safer route planner page the function of  buttons there was unclear. For example it took me some time to find where map for choosing pins directly on it is.
column12: I definitely would trust an app like this because if is deployed and in use of the municipalities, it can help a lot with maintenance, identifying the riskiest roads, new damages and will lead to less time of repairment.
column13: The application will be a lot useful if will be deployed in the near future, because it can help the municipalities to maintain high quality of the road, leading to less congestions, crashes and overall damage for the people cars.
column14: I think the prototype is great for now, and hope to be made fully operating in the future. Great work, no other comments.

column5:
Risk score is the risk calculated based on the damage detected on each image.
Green, yellow, and read represents the 3-level risk division - low, medium, high risk roads.
column11: Confusing while using the application I found the interface at the beginning, because it's not like a typical website, but more like an app which needs a guide to work with.
column12: I would use an automated system like this for routing, because this way I can avoid damages that can damage the vehicle I am driving in.
column13: The application will be more useful if it can be made on a mobile app like the typical routing maps. This way you can plan and avoid damages on real-time when driving.
column14: The app looks great, the UI can be improved. All it's functions are working. Overall, it's really good and hope to improve more soon.

column5: Green means low detected risk, orange means medium risk, and red means high risk. I understand the score as an estimate based on the damage detected in the images.
column11: I was unsure whether a road without a marker had been checked or whether there was no information available.
column12: I would use it to help choose a route, but I would want to know how recently the road images were collected.
column13: Show the date of the latest inspection for each road segment.
column14: Display the additional distance and estimated travel time beside the safer route.

column5: The colours show increasing levels of road damage risk. A higher score seems to indicate more damage or more serious damage.
column11: I did not immediately understand the damage class codes shown with the detections.
column12: I would consider the suggested route, especially if I could view the images supporting the assessment.
column13: Add short explanations and example images for each damage type.
column14: A brief introduction when opening the application would make it easier to use.

column5: Green represents lower risk, orange moderate risk, and red higher risk based on the detected road damage.
column11: The difference between detection confidence and the road risk score was unclear to me.
column12: I would use the results as guidance, but incorrect detections could affect my confidence in the recommended route.
column13: Allow users to report an incorrect detection or indicate that a pothole has been repaired.
column14: Reports of repaired damage should be checked before the map is updated.

column5: The score summarises the detected damage, and the colours divide the results into low, medium, and high risk.
column11: I was unsure how changing the risk-aversion setting would affect the recommended route.
column12: I would use it if the safer alternative only added a small amount of distance to my journey.
column13: Explain the route settings in simple language, becuase didn't know what the alpha set to 15k means.
column14: The app looks great, but the only thing that can be improved are the instructions on how to use it and what each threshold represents.

column5:
Green indicates low risk from detected damage, orange medium risk, and red high risk. I would not assume that a green road is completely free of hazards. 
Risk score I think is the summed risk based on all detected damages and their types.
column11: Some map markers on one of the roads were close together, making individual results difficult to select, but that was an individual case, because the damages were on a crossroad.
column12: I would consider it useful if the information were regularly updated and covered the roads I normally use.
column13: Improve the mobile layout and add location-based warnings before approaching damaged sections.
column14: Group nearby markers when zoomed out and show individual detections when zoomed in.
